scope: Synthetic CPU operator comparison, not model or device qualification

cases.name: distinct_rows
cases.purpose: Different activations must preserve independent projection outputs and chronological recurrent updates

cases.name: identical_rows
cases.purpose: Equal projection inputs must still share sequential recurrent state, not independent row copies

cases.name: swapped_rows
cases.purpose: Changing row order must be observable through causal history and state

cases.name: bf16_rounding
cases.purpose: Finite rounding-sensitive activations exercise the actual BF16 store boundaries

cases.name: nonzero_initial_state
cases.purpose: Nonzero history and recurrent state make accidental reset and independent-row execution observable

required_properties: Serial projection uses pinned original p33 per-lane arithmetic independently of paired implementation
Synthetic expanded Q6_K production layout and dimensions are explicit
Compare qkv and z projection bytes for both rows
Compare convolution outputs and history after row0 and after row1
Compare GDN outputs and BF16 persistent state after row0 and after row1
Active persistent state changes, so all-zero/inactive execution cannot satisfy the proof vacuously
An intentionally independent second-row state produces a different result and is rejected
No model payload, GPU, owner process, service or native device API is used
not_claimed: Exact selected GPU execution or full model output parity
Full-model attention, PLE or expert-cache chunk integration
A deliberately omitted interrow BF16 rounding negative control, unless separately implemented and observed to discriminate
